solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Half a bend? Halt, having to give way to motor

indicators.note: giving way means stepping aside so something else takes your place, so one part of the word is swapped out

parts.note: halt as a command or a stopping
the letters to be swapped out, taken as written
a motor is a car

explanation.surface: A driver at a bend is told to halt and give way to an oncoming vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: In STOP the letters TO give way to CAR. In heraldry a scarp is a diminutive of the bend sinister, half its width.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a scarp is a narrow diagonal band, the half-width diminutive of the bend sinister.

clue.text: Spotted old harvester cropping his last?

indicators.note: cropping trims something off, and 'his last' points to the final letter being trimmed

parts.note: the harvester or harvestman is a long-legged spider-like arachnid; harvest spider is another name

explanation.surface: Someone saw an old harvest worker who had cut his last field.
explanation.walkthrough: SPIDE is an old spelling of spied, so 'old' marks the definition as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Spide is an obsolete past tense of spy, so it means caught sight of, as spotted does.

clue.text: Early plane arrived, then left

parts.note: arrived means came
L is the abbreviation for left
joins the two parts in order

explanation.surface: An early-morning flight landed and then took off again.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sopwith Camel was a First World War biplane fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sopwith Camel was a celebrated fighter aircraft from the early days of military aviation.

clue.text: Sun cap, protective cover for antennae

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
a dome caps a building

explanation.surface: A sun hat doubles as protection for an insect's feelers.
explanation.definitionFit: A radome is the weatherproof dome housing a radar aerial, shielding it without blocking signals.

clue.text: Such common folk in Rome will appear translated in Berlin poems

definitions.text: Such common folk in Rome will appear translated in Berlin poems

indicators.note: translating turns words into another form, so these letters are turned into a new order
the clue says one group plus another will emerge from the fodder, so the second group is taken away to leave the first

parts.note: taken as written: the whole fodder
letters to be taken away from the fodder

explanation.surface: A German poet's verses will show the Roman lower orders once rendered into Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: BERLIN POEMS rearranges into the answer plus IN ROME, and the whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The plebs were the common people of ancient Rome, as distinct from the patricians.

clue.text: Necessary ingredient of baklava

indicators.note: an ingredient sits inside a dish, so the letters are found inside the next word

parts.note: the middle letters of the pastry name

explanation.surface: Something essential to the Middle Eastern pastry baklava.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Necessary' is used as a noun: the necessary, or necessary house, is an old euphemism for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A lav is a toilet, and 'the necessary' is an old euphemism for that same room.

clue.text: Typical of Bunter after Latin, describing his position in Remove?

indicators.note: 'after' places the piece named before it second, behind the piece that follows it in the clue

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Latin
Billy Bunter is nicknamed the Owl of the Remove, so owlish behaviour is typical of him

explanation.surface: A schoolboy's poor showing in Latin describes his rank in his form.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Bunter is the fat, bespectacled boy of the Greyfriars school stories; the Remove is his form, and he is the Owl of the Remove.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunter languishes near the bottom of his class, a humble, low-ranking position.

clue.text: E.g. ice and rains (cold) ruined the technical side of farming

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of its proper form, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: the abbreviation as written
taken as written
taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: Bad weather such as ice and cold rain wrecked the harvest, a blow to scientific farming.
explanation.definitionFit: Agriscience is the application of scientific method to agriculture.

clue.text: Cure for impotence, through proceeding by slow degrees (not dually)

parts.note: via means by way of, through

indicators.note: 'not' tells us to drop the following word's letters from the longer word before it

parts.note: an adverb for proceeding step by step
the letters removed, taken as written

explanation.surface: A treatment for impotence that works slowly, not two at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Viagra is the brand name of sildenafil, a drug that treats erectile dysfunction.

clue.text: Drink dad returned, become flavourless, stale

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters are read from the end

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does
pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: A drink brought back by Dad has gone flat and stale.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is an obsolete sense of a familiar word: in Chambers, to appal once meant to lose flavour or go flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers records an obsolete sense of appal meaning to pall, lose flavour or grow flat.

clue.text: Spicy dish Muslim maybe got stuck into at an end, once served up

indicators.note: in a down entry, 'up' means the letters run from bottom to top, the reverse order
getting stuck into something means going inside it, so one part is placed within another

parts.note: up means finished, as in 'time's up'
Ali is a common Muslim name

explanation.surface: A Muslim tucks into a spicy dish once it has been served.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilau is rice cooked in stock with spices, often with meat or vegetables.

clue.text: Playwright penning a line — some artist

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: Harold Pinter, the English dramatist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dramatist writes a single line, showing some artistic talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line' looks like a source of L, but it only completes the surface; 'penning' needs just the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter is one particular kind of artist, one who works in paint.

clue.text: Headless ghost in gest?

indicators.note: without a head means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a ghost is one that haunts

explanation.surface: A headless ghost appears in a medieval tale of deeds.
explanation.walkthrough: Aunter and gest are both old words: aunter for an adventure, gest for a deed or a tale of deeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunter is an archaic word for an adventure, and a gest is an adventurous exploit.

clue.text: Lines used by anglers on river in El Salvador

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

indicators.note: 'in' says the piece before it is placed inside the one after it

parts.note: ES is the international vehicle registration code for El Salvador
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Fishing lines in use on a river in Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: The on side in cricket is the half of the field behind the batter's legs, hence leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Leger lines are fishing lines weighted so the bait lies still on the bottom, a ledgering method.

clue.text: It impairs reasoned speech, making one confuse 'galop with aria'

indicators.note: to confuse things is to jumble them up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written; a galop is a lively dance
taken as written

explanation.surface: A speech disorder makes its sufferer mix up a dance and a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Paralogia is a thought disorder in which illogical reasoning shows itself in disjointed speech.

clue.text: Mobile facility that is limiting chat room monitor

indicators.note: limiting something puts bounds round it, so one piece sits on either side of the other

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for that is
a mod is a moderator who polices an online forum

explanation.surface: A phone feature that keeps an internet forum overseer in check.
explanation.definitionFit: i-mode was a Japanese mobile internet service, an early way to browse on a phone.

clue.text: West country sport, strangely lax, featured in press

indicators.note: a thing featured in another appears within it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: to wring is to squeeze or press

indicators.note: something done strangely is out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper report on a regional sport where the rules are oddly loose.
explanation.walkthrough: The West Country is south-west England; 'press' looks like journalism but means squeeze.
explanation.definitionFit: Wraxling is a dialect word for wrestling, a traditional sport of Devon and Cornwall.

clue.text: Carriage with room for one only? Poet pens 'sole' gibe, put out

definitions.text: Carriage with room for one only?

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the poet holds the other letters inside

parts.note: Dante Alighieri, the Italian poet

indicators.note: being put out means being disturbed, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet mocks a lone passenger who is annoyed at the carriage being a single seater.
explanation.walkthrough: The French name means 'disobliging', because the carriage would not take a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A désobligeante was an eighteenth-century carriage seating only one person.

clue.text: Short homily about associate making one sniffy?

indicators.note: 'about' means surrounding, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: ser. is an abbreviation of sermon, a homily
to mell is an old word meaning to mix or associate

explanation.surface: A brief sermon about mixing with others leaves someone looking disdainful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sniffy' usually means haughty, but here it means given to sniffing.
explanation.definitionFit: A smeller is one who smells or sniffs, read literally rather than as the haughty sense.

clue.text: One keen on sacking (from the sound) string player

indicators.note: judging by the sound means going by how the words are pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: a looter sacks towns, plundering them

explanation.surface: A musician seemingly fond of firing people, or of plunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacking' suggests dismissal, but here it means plundering.
explanation.definitionFit: A luter is a player of the lute, a plucked stringed instrument.

clue.text: Free from chemical accretions in bromides or bromines

indicators.note: 'in' says the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the middle one and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A chemistry note on cleaning deposits out of bromine compounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To desorb is to remove an adsorbed substance from a surface, freeing it of what has built up.

clue.text: It blooms in rocky environment, with wood as alternative

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
pine is a wood

explanation.surface: A plant flourishes among rocks, with woodland as another option.
explanation.definitionFit: Orpine is a stonecrop, a succulent with purple flowers that grows on rocky ground.

clue.text: Mobilized MD, i.e. with telegraph: 'That will respond to treatment'

indicators.note: something mobilized is set moving, so these letters move about

parts.note: taken as written
a cable is a telegram, a message sent by telegraph

explanation.surface: A doctor called up by telegram declares a patient treatable.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicable means curable, capable of being healed by medical treatment.

clue.text: Like pigeon? It's dodgy on diet

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable and out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pigeon on a diet seems a doubtful idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pigeon' is short for pigeon-toed, with feet turned inward.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pigeon-toed has feet turned inwards, which is exactly what in-toed describes.

clue.text: Dull old dimwit planting bean in ground with no depth

indicators.note: planting puts something into the soil, so one piece goes inside the other
depth is abbreviated by one letter, and 'with no' says that letter is dropped

parts.note: ground means land
urd is a kind of bean grown in India

explanation.surface: A foolish old man sows a bean in shallow soil.
explanation.walkthrough: D for depth is dropped from LAND before the bean goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurdan is an archaic term for a lazy, stupid person, a sluggish oaf.

clue.text: Build something to get children started in rotten tree

indicators.note: 'in' says the first piece is placed inside the second
something rotten has decayed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: 'started' points to the start of the word, its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Building a treehouse in a decayed tree to give the kids something to start on.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect a structure is to put it up, to construct it.

clue.text: Nelly I spotted on a steamer berthed in Cyprus

indicators.note: a ship berthed in a port sits inside it, so these pieces go within the next

parts.note: CY is the international code for Cyprus
taken as written
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A woman named Nelly is sighted aboard a ship docked in Cyprus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nelly' reads as a woman's name but is slang for an effeminate man.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelly and cissy are both dated, derogatory slang for an effeminate man.

clue.text: Not kosher — condition following introductions to the rabbi's experiment

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so only the opening letters are taken

parts.note: the opening letters of the three words
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A rabbi's test of whether some food is permitted under Jewish law.
explanation.definitionFit: Treif is Yiddish for food that is forbidden under Jewish dietary law, the opposite of kosher.

clue.text: What commander says on rising? 'Find a trumpeter'

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a Turkish commander, an aga, would say 'I'm aga'

explanation.surface: An officer's wake-up order to locate the bugler.
explanation.walkthrough: An aga is an Ottoman commander, so he would introduce himself as I'M AGA; the trumpeter is a bird, not a bugler.
explanation.definitionFit: The agami is a South American trumpeter, a crane-like bird named for its loud call.

clue.text: Source of amusement, hugging beside mattress

indicators.note: hugging wraps arms round something, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: fun is a source of amusement
to can mean beside or close to, as in 'cheek to cheek'

explanation.surface: Cuddling up next to someone on a bed is good fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A futon is a Japanese-style padded mattress laid on the floor or a frame.

clue.text: Meagre refrain

definitions.meaning: first meaning: thin or scanty, as an adjective
second meaning: to forbear or hold back from, as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: 'refrain' looks like a noun, a chorus, but is the verb, as in 'spare me the details'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an adjective for lean or scanty and as a verb for holding back from doing something.

clue.text: Spell with grey publishers? It doesn't attract those devoted to a party (13, two words)

definitions.text: It doesn't attract those devoted to a party

parts.note: in Scots and dialect a spell is a splinter of wood
gr. is an abbreviation for grey
OUP is Oxford University Press

explanation.surface: A grey party pamphlet that fails to win over the faithful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' suggests a period or a charm, but here it is the dialect word for a sliver.
explanation.definitionFit: A splinter group breaks away from a party, so loyal members do not join it.

clue.text: Aid in sharpening painting tint

parts.note: an oil is a painting done in oils
stone is a pale greyish-beige colour

explanation.surface: A tip for getting colours just right in a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: An oilstone is a whetstone lubricated with oil, used for honing blades.

clue.text: Some steady tables required where altars are found

indicators.note: 'some' means only part of what follows is taken

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Firm tables are needed to support church altars.
explanation.definitionFit: Adyta are the innermost sanctuaries of temples, the sacred places housing the altars.

clue.text: Medic savagely reversed duty cycle — his cuts are ruthless

indicators.note: acting savagely means violently, so the letters are torn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: this says the following piece is read from the end back

parts.note: a rota is a cycle of duties

explanation.surface: A doctor brutally reorganised the shift pattern, slashing staff mercilessly.
explanation.definitionFit: A decimator destroys a large part of something, originally killing one in ten, so his reductions are brutal.

clue.text: Cook e.g. slice of rubbery liver

indicators.note: a slice is a part cut from something, so the letters are a section of the words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A cook is told to serve, say, a slice of tough liver.
explanation.walkthrough: Beryl Cook was an English painter of comic, plump figures; 'Cook' looks like a kitchen instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Beryl is a first name, and Beryl Cook is a famous bearer of it.

clue.text: Fab dishes — eats away

indicators.note: sending something away removes it, so the named letters are taken out

parts.note: to dish an opponent is to defeat them
the letters removed, taken as written

explanation.surface: A food critic's verdict: the dishes are fabulous and the food is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Def is slang meaning excellent or cool, the same sense as fab.

clue.text: Italy's by no means combined (5, two words)

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy
none can mean not at all, as in 'none the wiser'

explanation.surface: Italy is in no way a unified whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things in one are rolled together into a single item, merged.
